Hi Mark. Last class you moved words to the front of a sentence to add weight. Today we go in the opposite direction, down to the smallest words in English, and one of them is not even there. English has a, it has the, and it has nothing at all, and that third option is the one Portuguese almost never gives you. Here is the mechanism. You use a or an the first time you mention something, because the person listening cannot identify it yet. A friend of mine plays that game. Then you switch to the, because now they can. The friend told me it takes forty hours. And you use no article at all when you mean the whole category rather than one member of it. Games are expensive. Music helps me concentrate. Portuguese puts an article in both of those and English does not, and that is the first trap. The second trap is choosing a or an by sound and not by spelling. An hour, because the H is silent. A university, because it starts with a Y sound. Say the word out loud and let your ear decide, never your eyes. One more group worth memorising. Some nouns take the because there is only one of them in the conversation: the internet, the news, the first game in the series. Others drop it because we mean the activity and not the building: go to school, go to bed, go to work. Before class, find any review in English and mark every the you can explain. See you on Wednesday, Mark.

Right, so you have never played it, which means I start from zero. It is a survival game, and survival games are a genre that people either love or never touch. You land on an island with nothing, and the island is different every time you start, so nobody can tell you what to expect. There is a crafting system, and the crafting system is where most people give up in the first hour. That is the learning curve everybody complains about, and honestly they are right. The first two hours are terrible. There is a grind too, and I am not going to pretend there is not, because you will spend a whole evening collecting wood. After that it becomes something else. It is not a shooter and it is not a story game. There are almost no cutscenes, so nothing ever stops to explain the plot to you. It is a sandbox, which means the game hands you the tools and then leaves. The soundtrack is the part nobody expects. There is silence for most of the time, and then the music comes back exactly when something is about to change. I have finished it three times, and the replay value is the real argument for it. It is not a mainstream franchise. It is niche, and it grew almost entirely by word of mouth, which is why you have never heard of it. If you want to get into it, skip the tutorial and let the game teach you.

First, ask whether you mean the whole category or one single member of it, because the whole category takes no article at all, and that is exactly where Portuguese pushes you the wrong way. Then, if you do mean one member, ask whether this is the first time it comes up in the conversation, because a first mention takes a or an. After that, if it is not the first mention, ask whether the person listening can now identify which one you mean, and if they can, the answer is the. Next, remember that you also use the when there is only one possible thing: the internet, the sun, the first game in the series. Finally, check a against an with your ear and not with your eyes, because an hour and a university both go against the spelling.
